summary: The Comoros issues a visa on arrival to virtually every nationality — travelers simply pay about EUR 30 (or the equivalent) at the airport in Moroni for a visa covering stays of up to 45 days, with no advance application needed.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Comoros
Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Comoros

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in the Comoros and have a blank page for the visa sticker and stamps.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Comoros

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (yellow card)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required only from travelers arriving from countries with a risk of yellow fever transmission. There is no yellow fever in the Comoros itself.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Comoros

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not an entry requirement, but medical facilities on the islands are basic and serious cases must be evacuated abroad — cover that includes medical evacuation is strongly recommended.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Comoros

onwardTicket.text: Immigration officers and airlines expect visitors to hold a confirmed onward or return ticket when arriving for the visa on arrival.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Comoros

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; officers may ask visitors to show means of support and accommodation details for their stay.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Comoros

payments.text: Bring your budget in cash, ideally euros. Cards are accepted almost nowhere, and the few ATMs in Moroni cannot be relied on to work with foreign cards. Euros are widely exchanged and often accepted directly for tourist services.

safety.text: The Comoros has little violent crime — petty theft is the main risk for visitors. Political demonstrations flare up occasionally, especially around elections, and should be avoided; inter-island boat travel in rough seas is a bigger everyday hazard than crime.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Comoros travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to October is the cooler, drier season — the best window for beaches, diving and climbing Mount Karthala; the November–April rains bring heat, humidity and a cyclone risk.

tips.text: Bring enough euros in cash for your whole stay plus the visa fee. Cards are close to useless on the islands and ATMs cannot be counted on.
Small ferries and speedboats between the islands can be overloaded and are risky in rough seas. Prefer domestic flights or larger vessels, and avoid night crossings.
Mount Karthala on Grande Comore is an active volcano. Check current conditions and take a local guide if you plan the overnight crater hike.
The Comoros is a conservative Muslim country. Dress modestly away from beach resorts, and be discreet with food and drink in public during Ramadan.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for the Comoros?
faq.answer: You need one, but not in advance — the Comoros grants a visa on arrival to virtually every nationality. Pay about EUR 30 at Prince Said Ibrahim airport in Moroni (cash) and you receive a visa covering stays of up to 45 days.

faq.question: How much does the Comoros visa on arrival cost?
faq.answer: Around EUR 30, payable in cash in euros or the equivalent in other major currencies or Comorian francs. Bring the exact amount if you can, and keep the receipt with your passport.

faq.question: Can I stay longer than 45 days in the Comoros?
faq.answer: The arrival visa covers stays of up to 45 days. For longer visits, ask about an extension at the immigration service in Moroni before your visa expires. Allow a few days for processing and confirm current fees locally.

faq.question: Can I pay by card in the Comoros?
faq.answer: Almost never. The islands run on cash. A few Moroni hotels may take cards, but ATMs are scarce and unreliable with foreign cards, so bring your full budget in euros and exchange as needed.
